docs.title: GitHub Workshop
docs.text:
GitHubWorkshop Content Summary

GitHubWorkshop is a workshop created by USSTIA for GitHub beginners. Starting with the basic concepts of GitHub and open source, the course gradually guides learners through finding, downloading, creating, and maintaining repositories, contributing through collaboration, and publishing websites, forming a complete practical path for getting started with GitHub.

Main Course Content Part One: Understanding GitHub and Finding Projects - Introduces the basic concepts of GitHub, Git, and open-source platforms. - Compares code hosting platforms such as GitHub, GitLab, Gitee, and Bitbucket. - Explains GitHub's advantages in terms of community size, collaboration mechanisms, tool ecosystem, and industry adoption. - Guides learners through registering a GitHub account. - Explains how to use search features to find projects. - Evaluates repositories based on dimensions such as Stars, Forks, Issues, commit history, contributors, License, README, and Releases. - Uses Insights, Commits, and Network to determine whether a project is still being maintained. - Distinguishes among three ways to obtain a project: Download ZIP, git clone, and downloading a Release. - Recommends learning resources such as freeCodeCamp, TheAlgorithms, the Awesome series, VS Code, and React. Part Two: Using Repositories and Participating in Collaboration - Creates public or private repositories and configures the README, .gitignore, and License. - Uploads files through the web interface or uses Git to complete add, commit, and push operations. - Introduces common open-source licenses such as MIT, Apache 2.0, GPL, and BSD. - Explains what a Fork is and when to use one. - Demonstrates the standard open-source contribution workflow: Fork → Clone → Create a branch → Modify and commit → Push → Pull Request → Review - Explains how to submit high-quality Issues and continuously update a PR based on review feedback. - Advises using git add -f with caution to avoid accidentally committing files excluded by .gitignore. - Introduces how to create, edit, upload, and delete files through the GitHub web interface. - Explains the purpose and basic structure of a README, as well as commonly used Markdown syntax. - Guides learners through publishing a repository as a static website with GitHub Pages.

Summary The core goal of this workshop is to help beginners progress from "understanding GitHub" to "using GitHub to participate in real-world projects." By the end of the workshop, participants should be able to independently find and evaluate open-source projects, create and maintain repositories, choose appropriate licenses, use Git for basic version control, collaborate through Issues and Pull Requests, and showcase projects with GitHub Pages.

The main course content now covers the complete beginner workflow, but parts of the homepage and README still retain descriptions from the earlier Workshop Template and do not fully match the actual GitHub Workshop course content.

docs.title: A brief introduction of GitHub
docs.text: Towards GitHub

docs.title: Part One: Introduction: Towards GitHub
docs.text: here is the logo of GitHub

docs.title: 1. What Is GitHub?
docs.text:
GitHub is a code hosting and collaboration platform built on the Git version control system. It launched in 2008 and was acquired by Microsoft in 2018. Simply put, it is a website for "storing code and writing code with others."

Tip

GitHub is different form git. GitHub is a open-source platform and the repositories of it is based on git. However, GitHub is very "open". You can find some unexpected things here even they have nothing to do with coding. Theoretically, you can put anything you want.

some interesting examples

  • Free Programming Books: A community-maintained collection of free programming books and learning resources.

  • HowToCook: A programmer's guide to cooking at home, with clear, step-by-step recipes.

  • No Code: A humorous project about writing no code and deploying nowhere. This popular "empty repository" still contains a README and other files.

  • 科技爱好者周刊 (Tech Enthusiast Weekly): A weekly technology newsletter that welcomes reader submissions through Issues.

  • OSSU Computer Science: A community-organized curriculum for teaching yourself computer science.

In addition to hosting code, GitHub also provides features such as Issues (issue tracking), Actions (automation), Pages (static website hosting), Wiki (documentation), and Codespaces (cloud development environments). It has evolved into a complete developer community and engineering collaboration ecosystem.

docs.title: 2. What Is an Open-Source Platform?
docs.text:
An open-source platform is a data hosting platform where source code is made public. It typically hosts a variety of open-source projects.

Open-source platforms usually use licenses to prevent the misuse of open-source content.

Well-known (or useful) open-source platforms:

  • GitHub Currently the world's largest open-source community platform with the strongest ecosystem

  • Gitee A viable domestic alternative to GitHub in China

  • Hugging Face An open-source platform for AI models

docs.title: 3. What Open-Source Platforms Are Available, and What Are GitHub's Advantages?
docs.text:
Common code hosting / open-source platforms:

Platform Features GitHub The world's largest and most active community, with the most comprehensive ecosystem GitLab Offers self-hosting (deploying it yourself) and strong integrated DevOps capabilities Bitbucket Developed by Atlassian and integrates well with Jira and other tools Gitee A Chinese platform with fast access and a Chinese-language community SourceForge A long-established open-source project hosting platform GitCode A relatively new code hosting platform in China

GitHub's core advantages:

  1. The largest community: Nearly all well-known open-source projects (such as Linux-related resources, VS Code, React, Vue, and TensorFlow) are hosted on GitHub, where developers, organizations, and companies are highly concentrated.
  2. "Social Coding": Features such as Stars, Forks, Follows, and PRs make both code and developers discoverable and open to collaboration.
  3. The richest ecosystem: GitHub Actions (automation), GitHub Pages (free website hosting), GitHub Copilot (an AI coding assistant), Codespaces, and other supporting services are all readily available.
  4. Generous free tier: A free personal account can create unlimited public repositories (private repositories also have usage limits), which is sufficient for personal learning and small teams.
  5. The de facto standard: The combination of git and GitHub has effectively become an industry-standard workflow. Job hunting, contributing to open source, and reading high-quality source code often begin with GitHub.

docs.title: 4. Practice: Register a GitHub Account
docs.text:
Goal: Have your own GitHub account and be able to sign in and create repositories.

Steps:

  1. Open a browser and visit https://github.com.
  2. Click Sign up in the upper-right corner.
  3. Follow the prompts and enter:
  4. Email: Use an email address that you check regularly and can keep using long-term;
  5. Password: Use at least 8 characters; a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols is recommended;
  6. Username: This will appear in your profile URL, https://github.com/<username>. Choose a short, recognizable, and professional name, such as the pinyin spelling of your name or a commonly used nickname;
  7. Click Create account. GitHub will send a verification email to the address you provided.
  8. Open your email and click Verify email address to complete verification.
  9. Return to GitHub to access your profile page.

Recommendations after registration:

  • Configure SSH to make it easier to clone GitHub repositories with git

docs.title: Section Two: Searching on GitHub (How to Find Useful Repositories)
docs.text: The search bar is at the top; the largest input box is not the search bar

docs.title: 5. How to Evaluate a Repository
docs.text:
When you encounter an unfamiliar repository, you can quickly assess whether it is worth using, learning from, or contributing to based on the following dimensions:

Dimension Where to Look Description Stars ⭐ in the upper-right corner of the repository page Similar to favorites/likes and the most visible indicator of popularity; generally, more is better Forks Next to Stars The number of times the repository has been copied for further development, indicating how many people have built upon it Watchers Repository page The number of people following the repository, indicating sustained interest Issues Issues tab Check the number of issues and whether maintainers respond to and resolve them promptly Latest commit time File list / Commits Indicates whether the project is still being maintained Number of contributors Insights → Contributors More contributors generally indicate healthier collaboration License Repository root / About section on the right Determines whether and how you may use the code README quality Repository home page Check whether it provides clear introductions, installation instructions, and usage guidance Releases / Tags Releases tab Check whether stable versions exist and how frequently new versions are released

docs.title: 6. How to Determine a Repository's Current Status
docs.text:
"Status" mainly refers to whether a project is currently active, maintained, or abandoned. You can determine this by:

Reviewing the content under Insights

1. Pulse: Check whether the repository has been maintained recently

Pulse summarizes recent Pull Requests, Issues, and commit activity in the repository. If people are still regularly submitting code and handling issues, the project is usually still actively maintained.

2. Check Contributors

The Contributors page shows the number of participants and their contribution trends. If there are many contributors and people are still contributing recently, the project's collaboration and maintenance are relatively healthy.

3. Check commits

Review the date of the most recent commit and the commit frequency to determine whether the code is still being updated. A long period without new commits may mean that the project is stable, or it may mean that maintenance has stopped; check Issues and Releases as well.

4. Check Network

The Network graph shows commit relationships and branch changes between the repository and its forks. If the original repository has stopped updating but one of its forks remains actively developed, you can follow that fork instead.

docs.title: 7. How to Download a Repository's Source Code
docs.text:
There are several common methods. Choose one based on your needs:

Method 1: Download a ZIP file directly (the simplest option, suitable if you only want to view the code)

  1. Open the repository page and click the green Code button.
  2. Select Download ZIP from the drop-down menu.
  3. Extract the archive to obtain the complete source code from the repository's current default branch.

Disadvantage: It does not include Git history and cannot pull future updates, so it is suitable for obtaining the code only once.

Method 2: git clone (recommended if you want to use or further develop the code)

After installing Git on your computer, open a terminal and run:

Bash
git clone https://github.com/<username>/<repository-name>.git

For example, clone a repository commonly used as an example in this project:

Bash
git clone https://github.com/github/gitignore.git

After cloning, you will have the complete repository and its version history locally. You can later use git pull to retrieve updates from the remote repository.

  • HTTPS (https://github.com/...): Easy to configure and broadly compatible; recommended for beginners.
  • SSH (git@github.com:...): Requires configuring an SSH key first. It is faster and suitable for frequent pushes, but the setup is slightly more complex.

Method 3: Download a Release (suitable for software that can be run directly)

If you only want an executable file or installer for a piece of software, do not download the source code. Instead, open the Releases page and download the release package for your platform (Windows / macOS / Linux), such as an .exe, .dmg, or .zip file.

docs.title: 8. Some Useful Repositories
docs.text:
The following public repositories are very useful for learning and getting started. Search for and explore them according to your interests:

Learning

  • free-programming-books-zh: A collection of free Chinese programming books.
  • freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp: An open-source platform offering free programming courses and exercises.
  • TheAlgorithms: A collection of data structures and algorithms implemented in various programming languages.

Resource Collections (Awesome Lists)

  • awesome: A central collection of curated resource lists covering a wide variety of topics.
  • awesome-chinese / various awesome-xxx repositories: Curated resource lists organized by topic, making it easy to follow a trail of useful resources.

Engineering / Tools

  • github/gitignore: A collection of .gitignore templates for various languages and environments.
  • vscode: The source code of Microsoft's open-source editor, VS Code; suitable for studying a large-scale project.
  • vuejs/vue and facebook/react: The source code of mainstream front-end frameworks.

Practice (based on this section):

  1. Search for a topic that interests you
  2. Find a well-maintained repository
  3. Download some useful code

docs.title: Using a GitHub Repository
docs.text: Author: Zhang Junming

docs.title: 1. How to Create a Repository
docs.text:
1. Log in to github.com, click the + icon in the upper right corner, and select New repository.
  2. Fill in the information:
  3. Repository name: Required, e.g., my-first-project.
  4. Description: Optional, a brief explanation of what the repository is for.
  5. Public / Private: A public repository can be viewed by anyone; a private repository can only be viewed by you and invited people.
  6. Add a README file: Recommended, automatically generates a README.md.
  7. Add .gitignore: Optional, ignores files that don't need to be uploaded based on your language (C/C++, Python, etc.).
  8. Choose a license: Optional, select an open-source license (see Section 2).
  9. Click Create repository to finish creating.

After creating it, you have two ways to put code into the repository: - Web operations: Click Add file → Upload files to drag and drop directly. - Local Git: Copy the repository address and run in the terminal:

Bash
git clone https://github.com/your-username/repository-name.git
# After placing files inside
git add .
git commit -m "first commit"
git push

Of course, if your computer has not been configured with a username and email, you cannot commit, so you need to (if you don't want a global configuration and only want to configure this one repository, remove --global):

Bash
git config --global user.name <your name, come up with one yourself>
git config --global user.email <email>
git config --list # used to confirm your configuration status

docs.title: 2. What Is a License
docs.text:
A License is a legal statement that specifies how others may use your code. It is an important part of open-source projects:

License Features Applicable Scenarios MIT The most permissive; others can use, modify, and commercialize freely, only needing to retain the copyright notice Most personal projects Apache 2.0 Permissive + explicit patent grant Enterprises, needing patent protection GPL Strong "infectiousness"; if you use it, you must also open-source Want derivative projects to be open-source too BSD Similar to MIT, with slightly more clauses Academic projects

Key points: - No license means "all rights reserved" by default; others cannot legally copy or modify your code. - How to add: Select it directly when creating the repository, or later click Add file → Create new file, write the file name as LICENSE.txt, and GitHub will automatically provide template options.

docs.title: 3. How to Fork a Repository
docs.text:
Fork means completely copying someone else's repository to your own account, after which you can modify it freely without affecting the original repository.

  1. Open the repository page you want to fork.
  2. Click the Fork button in the upper right corner (usually next to Star).
  3. Select the target account (usually yourself) and click Create fork.
  4. After completion, a repository with the same name will appear under your account, marked "forked from original author/original repository".

After getting the fork, clone it locally:

Bash
git clone https://github.com/your-username/repository-name.git
Uses: wanting to do secondary development based on someone else's project, learn the source code, or prepare to submit a Pull Request to the original project (see Section 4).

docs.title: 4. How to Contribute to a Repository
docs.text:
The core process of contributing is Fork → Modify → Pull Request (PR):

  1. Fork the target repository (Section 3).
  2. Clone your fork locally: Bash
    git clone https://github.com/your-username/repository-name.git
cd repository-name
  3. Create a new branch to avoid modifying main directly: Bash
    git checkout -b <branch name>
  4. Modify the code or documentation, then commit: (I believe you are already very familiar with these from 151 or 101) Bash
    git add .
git commit -m "Describe your changes"
git push origin my-feature

[!] Note that, suppose your .gitignore ignores .o files, but you still do:

Bash
git add -f main.o
This will force the addition and treat main.o as a tracked file, so try not to write -f.
  1. Go back to your fork page on GitHub and click Contribute → Open pull request.
  2. Clearly describe what you changed and why (be detailed), then click Create pull request.
  3. Wait for the original repository maintainer to review; they may give feedback, and you can continue to modify and push to update the same PR.

Supplement: - If you just find a bug or want to make a suggestion, you can directly submit a New issue on the repository's Issues page. This is also a way to contribute. At the same time, your Issue should not be just one or two lines; instead, it should explain your suggestion, bug description, and your version, environment, etc. as detailed as possible. - If the original repository gives you write permission, you can skip the fork and directly create a branch, make changes, and submit a PR.

docs.title: 5. How to Quickly Edit Content in a Repository
docs.text:
You don't need local Git; you can quickly edit directly on the web page:

  1. Open a file in the repository and click the pencil icon (Edit this file) in the upper right corner.
  2. Modify the content directly in the edit box.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of the page, write a short commit message, and choose to commit to the current branch or a new branch.
  4. Click Commit changes to save.

Other web shortcuts: - New file: Add file → Create new file. - Upload file: Add file → Upload files. - Delete file: Open the file → trash can icon in the upper right corner → Commit.

Note: Web editing is suitable for small changes (changing documentation, fixing one line of code). For large changes that require local compilation and testing, the local Git workflow in Section 4 is still more suitable.

docs.title: 6. How to Use README
docs.text:
README.md is the documentation displayed by default on the homepage after opening the repository, written in Markdown. It is the "first business card" for others to understand your project.

A good README usually includes: - Project introduction: One sentence explaining what this project does. - Installation method: Environment dependencies, how to install. - Usage method: How to run, example code. - License / Contribution method: Point to LICENSE or explain how to participate.

Common Markdown syntax:

Markdown
# Level 1 heading
## Level 2 heading
- List item
**Bold**, *italic*
`inline code`
[link text](URL)
![image description](image URL)
```
code block
```

How to create: Check "Add a README file" when creating a new repository, or later click Add file → Create new file and write the file name as README.md.

docs.title: 7. How to Build a Web Page Corresponding to the Repository (GitHub Pages)
docs.text:
GitHub Pages can turn a repository into a free hosted static website.

  1. Open the repository → Settings → Pages on the left.
  2. Under Build and deployment, select Deploy from a branch for Source.
  3. Select the branch (usually main) and directory (root directory / or /docs), and click Save.
  4. After a few dozen seconds, the page will give you your URL: https://your-username.github.io/repository-name/.

Content sources: - The simplest approach: Place an index.html in the repository root directory; this is the homepage. - You can also use Jekyll (built into GitHub) to automatically generate blog-style pages by selecting a theme. - There is also a "user homepage" type: Create a repository named your-username.github.io, and the URL will be https://your-username.github.io/.

docs.title: 8. The Practical Process Corresponding to the Above Steps
docs.text: First use Step 1 to create a repository → use Steps 2 and 6 to clarify the project → use Step 3 to Fork when you need someone else's code → follow Step 4's PR when participating in collaboration → use Step 5 for small daily changes → once the project matures, you can use Step 7 to build a web page for display.

docs.title: GitHub Workshop
docs.text:
GitHubWorkshop 内容摘要

GitHubWorkshop 是一套由 USSTIA 制作、面向 GitHub 初学者的workshop。课程从 GitHub 和开源的基本概念出发，逐步引导学习者完成仓库查找、下载、创建、维护、协作贡献和网站发布，形成一条完整的 GitHub 入门实践路径。

课程主要内容 第一部分：认识 GitHub 与寻找项目 - 介绍 GitHub、Git 和开源平台的基本概念。 - 对比 GitHub、GitLab、Gitee、Bitbucket 等代码托管平台。 - 说明 GitHub 在社区规模、协作机制、工具生态和行业应用方面的优势。 - 指导学习者注册 GitHub 账号。 - 讲解如何使用搜索功能寻找项目。 - 从 Star、Fork、Issue、提交记录、贡献者、License、README 和 Release 等维度评价仓库。 - 通过 Insights、Commits 和 Network 判断项目是否仍在维护。 - 区分 Download ZIP、git clone 和下载 Release 三种获取项目的方式。 - 推荐 freeCodeCamp、TheAlgorithms、Awesome 系列、VS Code、React 等学习资源。 第二部分：使用仓库与参与协作 - 创建公开或私有仓库，配置 README、.gitignore 和 License。 - 使用网页上传文件，或通过 Git 完成 add、commit 和 push。 - 介绍 MIT、Apache 2.0、GPL、BSD 等常见开源许可证。 - 解释 Fork 的含义及其适用场景。 - 演示标准开源贡献流程： Fork → Clone → 创建分支 → 修改并提交 → Push → Pull Request → Review - 说明如何提交高质量 Issue，以及如何根据审查意见持续更新 PR。 - 提醒谨慎使用 git add -f，避免误提交被 .gitignore 排除的文件。 - 介绍 GitHub 网页端的新建、编辑、上传和删除文件功能。 - 讲解 README 的作用、基本结构和常用 Markdown 语法。 - 指导使用 GitHub Pages 将仓库发布为静态网站。

总结 这个wksp的核心目标，是帮助初学者完成从“认识 GitHub”到“能够使用 GitHub 参与实际项目”的过渡。学习结束后，参与者应能独立寻找并判断开源项目、创建和维护仓库、正确选择许可证、使用 Git 完成基本版本管理、通过 Issue 和 Pull Request 参与协作，并使用 GitHub Pages展示项目。

当前课程主体已经覆盖完整的入门流程，但部分首页和 README 仍保留早期 Workshop Template 的模板描述，与实际 GitHub Workshop 课程内容并不完全一致。

docs.title: 1. GitHub 是什么（1min）
docs.text:
GitHub 是一个基于 Git 版本控制系统构建的代码托管与协作平台，于 2008 年上线，2018 年被微软收购。简单来说，它是一个"存放代码、和别人一起写代码"的网站。

除了托管代码，GitHub 还提供 Issue（问题追踪）、Actions（自动化）、Pages（静态网站托管）、Wiki（文档）、Codespaces（云端开发环境） 等功能，已经发展成一个完整的开发者社区和工程协作生态。

docs.title: 2. 什么是开源平台（4min）
docs.text:
开源平台，即是公开源代码的数据托管平台，通常承载了各种不同的开源项目。

开源平台通常会设置许可证，避免开源内容滥用。

经典（或者有用）的开源平台：

  • GitHub 目前世界上最大也是生态最好的开源社区平台
  • Gitee 国内一个可行的作为GitHub的代替平台
  • Hugging Face AI 模型的开源平台

docs.title: 3. 开源平台有哪些，GitHub 在其中的优势是什么（1min）
docs.text:
常见的代码托管 / 开源平台：

平台 特点 GitHub 全球最大、社区最活跃，生态最完善 GitLab 提供自托管（自己部署）方案，DevOps 一体化能力强 Bitbucket 由 Atlassian 出品，与 Jira 等工具集成好 Gitee（码云） 国内平台，访问速度快，中文社区 SourceForge 老牌开源项目托管站 GitCode 国内较新的开源托管平台

GitHub 的核心优势：

  1. 社区规模最大：几乎所有知名开源项目（如 Linux 相关资料、VS Code、React、Vue、TensorFlow 等）都托管在 GitHub 上，开发者、组织和公司高度聚集。
  2. "社交化编程"（Social Coding）：通过 Star（收藏/点赞）、Fork（复刻）、Follow（关注）、PR 等方式，让代码和开发者都"可被发现、可被协作"。
  3. 生态最丰富：GitHub Actions（自动化）、GitHub Pages（免费网站托管）、GitHub Copilot（AI 编程助手）、Codespaces 等配套服务一应俱全。
  4. 免费额度友好：个人免费账号即可创建无限公开仓库（私有仓库也有限额），对个人学习和小型团队足够使用。
  5. 事实上的标准：git + GitHub 的用法几乎成为行业通行做法，找工作、参与开源、阅读优秀源码大多从 GitHub 开始。

docs.title: 4. 实践：注册 GitHub 账号（10min）
docs.text:
目标：拥有一个自己的 GitHub 账号，能登录、能创建仓库。

步骤：

  1. 打开浏览器，访问 https://github.com。
  2. 点击右上角 Sign up（注册）。
  3. 按提示依次填写：
  4. 邮箱：建议用常用、可长期使用的邮箱；
  5. 密码：至少 8 位，建议包含大小写字母、数字和符号；
  6. 用户名（Username）：会出现在你的主页地址 https://github.com/<用户名> 中，建议用简短、易识别、专业的名字（如姓名拼音或常用昵称）；
  7. 点击 Create account，GitHub 会向你填写的邮箱发送一封验证邮件。
  8. 登录邮箱，点击邮件中的 Verify email address 完成验证。
  9. 回到 GitHub，即可进入你的个人主页。

完成注册后的建议：

  • 配置SSH：便于使用git克隆GitHub上的仓库

docs.title: 第二部分　GitHub 的搜索（怎么找到有用的仓库）（25min）
docs.text: 搜索栏在上方，那个最大的输入框不是搜索栏

docs.title: 5. 怎么评价一个仓库（3min）
docs.text:
面对一个陌生仓库，可以从以下几个维度快速评估它"值不值得用 / 学 / 参与"：

维度 在哪里看 说明 Star 数 仓库主页右上角 ⭐ 相当于"收藏/点赞"数，是受欢迎程度最直观的指标，一般越多越好 Fork 数 Star 旁边 被复刻的次数，反映有多少人基于它做二次开发 Watch 数 仓库主页 关注人数，反映持续关注度 Issue 情况 Issues 标签页 看 issue 数量、是否有维护者及时回复和处理 最近提交时间 文件列表 / Commits 判断项目是否还在维护 Contributor 数量 Insights → Contributors 参与人数越多，说明协作越健康 License 仓库根目录 / 右侧 About 决定你能不能用、怎么用这份代码 README 质量 仓库首页 是否有清晰的介绍、安装和使用说明 Release / Tag Releases 标签页 是否有稳定版本号，是否频繁发版

docs.title: 6. 如何判断一个仓库现在的状态（3min）
docs.text:
"状态"主要指这个项目目前是活跃、维护中，还是已经弃坑。判断方法：

观察insight中的内容

  1. Pulse：检查这个仓库最近是否有人维护

Pulse 会汇总仓库近期的 Pull Request、Issue 和提交活动。若最近持续有人提交代码、处理问题，通常说明项目仍在活跃维护。

  1. 看 Contributor

Contributors 页面可以看到参与者数量及各自的贡献趋势。贡献者较多且近期仍有人持续贡献，说明项目的协作和维护相对健康。

  1. 看 commits

查看最近一次提交时间以及提交频率，判断代码是否还在更新。长期没有新提交可能表示项目已稳定，也可能已经停止维护，需要结合 Issue 和 Release 一起判断。

  1. 看 network

Network 图展示仓库及其 Fork 之间的提交关系和分支变化。如果原仓库更新停滞，但某个 Fork 仍在活跃开发，可以进一步关注该 Fork。

docs.title: 7. 怎么下载一个仓库的源代码（5min）
docs.text:
有几种常用方式，按场景选择：

方式一：直接下载 ZIP（最简单，适合只想看代码）

  1. 进入仓库主页，点击绿色的 Code 按钮。
  2. 在下拉菜单中选择 Download ZIP。
  3. 解压后即可得到该仓库当前主分支的完整源代码。

缺点：不含 Git 历史记录，也无法后续拉取更新，适合一次性获取代码。

方式二：git clone（推荐，适合要使用/二次开发）

在电脑上安装 Git 后，打开终端（Terminal），执行：

Bash
git clone https://github.com/<用户名>/<仓库名>.git

例如克隆本项目常用的示例：

Bash
git clone https://github.com/github/gitignore.git

克隆完成后，本地就拥有该仓库的完整内容与版本历史，之后可用 git pull 获取远端更新。

  • HTTPS 方式（https://github.com/...）：配置简单，通用性最好，推荐初学者使用。
  • SSH 方式（git@github.com:...）：需要先配置 SSH 密钥，速度更快、适合频繁推送，但配置稍复杂。

方式三：下载 Release 发行版（适合下载可直接运行的软件）

如果只是想下载某个软件的可执行文件或安装包，不要下载源码，而是进入 Releases 页面，下载对应平台（Windows / macOS / Linux）的 .exe、.dmg、.zip 等发行包。

docs.title: 8. 一些有用的仓库（10min）
docs.text:
以下是一些对学习和入门非常有帮助的公开仓库，可按兴趣搜索并实践：

学习类

  • free-programming-books-zh：免费的中文编程书籍合集。
  • freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp：开源的免费编程学习课程与练习平台。
  • TheAlgorithms：用各种语言实现的数据结构与算法合集。

资源合集类（Awesome 系列）

  • awesome：各种主题的"精选资源清单"总入口。
  • awesome-chinese / 各类 awesome-xxx：按主题整理的优质资源列表，非常适合按图索骥。

工程/工具类

  • github/gitignore：各种语言和环境的 .gitignore 模板合集。
  • vscode：微软的开源编辑器 VS Code 源码，适合阅读大型项目。
  • vuejs/vue、facebook/react：主流前端框架源码。

实践环节（结合本部分内容）：

  1. 搜索一个感兴趣的话题
  2. 找到一个运行良好的仓库
  3. 下载一个有用的代码

docs.title: Github 仓库的使用
docs.text: 作者： 张峻铭 日期： 2026.11.01 状态： 草稿

docs.title: 1. 如何创建一个仓库
docs.text:
1. 登录 github.com，点击右上角的 + 图标，选择 New repository（新建仓库）。
  2. 填写信息：
  3. Repository name（仓库名）：必填，例如 my-first-project。
  4. Description（描述）：可选，简单说明这个仓库是干什么的。
  5. Public / Private：公开仓库任何人都能看；私有仓库只有自己和被邀请的人能看。
  6. Add a README file：建议勾选，自动生成一个 README.md。
  7. Add .gitignore：可选，根据你用的语言（C/C++、Python 等）忽略不需要上传的文件。
  8. Choose a license：可选，选择开源许可证（见第 2 节）。
  9. 点击 Create repository 完成创建。

创建之后，你有两种方式往仓库里放代码： - 网页操作：点 Add file → Upload files 直接拖拽上传。 - 本地 Git：复制仓库地址，在终端执行：

Bash
git clone https://github.com/你的用户名/仓库名.git
# 放入文件后
git add .
git commit -m "first commit"
git push

当然如果你的电脑没有配置过 username 和 email， 你无法 commit， 所以你需要 ( 如果你不想全局配置，只想配置这一个仓库，删掉 --global)：

Bash
git config --global user.name <你的名字，自己想一个>
git config --global user.email <邮箱>
git config --list #用于确认你的配置状态

docs.title: 2. License 是什么
docs.text:
License（许可证） 是一份法律声明，规定别人可以怎样使用你的代码。它是开源项目里很重要的一部分：

许可证 特点 适用场景 MIT 最宽松，别人可以随便用、改、商用，只需保留版权声明 大多数个人项目 Apache 2.0 宽松 + 明确专利授权 企业、需要专利保护 GPL “传染性”强，用了它就必须同样开源 希望衍生项目也开源 BSD 类似 MIT，条款略多 学院派项目

要点： - 没有 license 是默认“保留所有权利”，别人不能合法地复制或修改你的代码。 - 添加方法：创建仓库时直接选择，或之后点 Add file → Create new file，把文件名写成 LICENSE.txt，GitHub 会自动提供模板选择。

docs.title: 3. 如何 Fork 一个仓库
docs.text:
Fork（分叉） 就是把别人的仓库完整复制一份到你自己的账号下，之后你可以自由修改，而不会影响原仓库。

  1. 打开你想 fork 的仓库页面。
  2. 点击右上角的 Fork 按钮（一般在 Star 旁边）。
  3. 选择目标账号（通常就是你自己），点击 Create fork。
  4. 完成后，你账号下就会出现一份同名仓库，标注了 “forked from 原作者/原仓库”。

拿到 fork 后，把它克隆到本地：

Bash
git clone https://github.com/你的用户名/仓库名.git

用途：想在别人项目基础上二次开发、学习源码、或者准备给原项目提 Pull Request（见第 4 节）。

docs.title: 4. 如何 Contribute 一个仓库
docs.text:
贡献的核心流程是 Fork → 修改 → Pull Request（PR）：

  1. Fork 目标仓库（第 3 节）。
  2. 克隆自己的 fork 到本地：
Bash
git clone https://github.com/你的用户名/仓库名.git
cd 仓库名
  1. 新建一个分支，避免直接在 main 上改：
Bash
git checkout -b my-feature
  1. 修改代码或文档，然后提交：（相信这些在 151 or 101 已经很熟练了）

Bash
git add .
git commit -m "描述你的改动"
git push origin my-feature
[!] 需要注意的是, 假设你的.gitignore里屏蔽了.o文件，但是仍然： Bash
git add -f main.o
会导致强制添加，并把main.o当成已追踪文件，所以尽量不要写 -f
  1. 回到 GitHub 上你的 fork 页面，点击 Contribute → Open pull request。
  2. 写清楚你改了什么、为什么改 (详细一点)，然后点 Create pull request。
  3. 等待原仓库维护者 review（审查）；他们可能会提意见，你继续修改并 push 即可更新同一个 PR。

补充： - 如果只是发现 bug 或提建议，可以直接在仓库的 Issues 页面提交 New issue，这也是贡献的一种方式,同时，你的 Issue 不要一两行带过，而是应该尽可能详细地阐明你的建议，bug的描述，和你的版本，环境等。 - 如果原仓库给了你写权限，可以跳过 fork，直接建分支改完提 PR。

docs.title: 5. 如何快速编辑一个仓库里的内容
docs.text:
不需要本地 Git，直接在网页上就能快速改：

  1. 打开仓库里的某个文件，点击右上角的铅笔图标（Edit this file）。
  2. 在编辑框里直接修改内容。
  3. 滚动到页面底部，写一句简短的提交说明（Commit message），选择提交到当前分支或新分支。
  4. 点 Commit changes 保存。

其他网页快捷操作： - 新建文件：Add file → Create new file。 - 上传文件：Add file → Upload files。 - 删除文件：打开文件 → 右上角垃圾桶图标 → Commit。

注意：网页编辑适合小改动（改个文档、修一行代码）。如果是大改动、需要本地编译测试，还是用第 4 节里的本地 Git 流程更合适。

docs.title: 6. README 怎么使用
docs.text:
README.md 是仓库打开后默认展示在首页的说明文档，用 Markdown 编写。它是别人了解你项目的“第一张名片”。

一份好的 README 通常包含： - 项目简介：一句话说明这个项目是做什么的。 - 安装方法：环境依赖、如何安装。 - 使用方法：怎么运行、示例代码。 - 许可证 / 贡献方式：指向 LICENSE 或说明如何参与。

常用 Markdown 语法：

Markdown
# 一级标题
## 二级标题
- 列表项
**加粗**、*斜体*
`行内代码`
[链接文字](网址)
![图片描述](图片地址)

```代码块```

创建方法：新建仓库时勾选 “Add a README file”，或之后点 Add file → Create new file，文件名写 README.md。

docs.title: 7. 怎么建立仓库对应的网页（GitHub Pages）
docs.text:
GitHub Pages 可以把仓库变成一个免费托管的静态网站。

  1. 打开仓库 → Settings → 左侧 Pages。
  2. 在 Build and deployment 下，Source 选择 Deploy from a branch。
  3. 选择分支（通常选 main）和目录（根目录 / 或 /docs），点 Save。
  4. 等几十秒，页面会给出你的网址：https://你的用户名.github.io/仓库名/。

内容来源： - 最简单的做法：在仓库根目录放一个 index.html，这就是首页。 - 也可以使用 Jekyll（GitHub 内置支持）来自动生成博客风格的页面，选一个主题即可。 - 还有一种“用户主页”型：创建名为 你的用户名.github.io 的仓库，网址就是 https://你的用户名.github.io/。

docs.title: 8. 以上步骤对应的实践过程
docs.text: 先用第 1 步建仓库 → 用第 2、6 步把项目弄清楚 → 需要别人代码时用第 3 步 Fork → 参与协作时走第 4 步 PR → 平时小改动用第 5 步 → 项目成熟后可以用第 7 步搭个网页展示。
